India. The world's seventh-largest country by area and second-most populous, with a civilization spanning over five thousand years. It is the birthplace of Hinduism and Buddhism, home to the Vedic philosophy that shaped world thought, and the site of the Taj Mahal. India's cultures, religions, and intellectual traditions have profoundly influenced Asia and the world.

The Vedic civilization from around fifteen hundred to five hundred BCE produced the Vedas, the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism, establishing philosophies of karma, dharma, and reincarnation that influenced billions. Hinduism, one of the world's major religions, emerged in India and encompasses diverse practices, deities, and philosophical schools unified by belief in eternal truth called Satya and cyclical time. Buddhism, founded in India by the Buddha in the fifth century BCE, originated as a reaction to Vedic Brahmanism and spread across Asia, becoming one of the world's major religions.

The Taj Mahal, built in the seventeenth century by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan as a mausoleum for his wife, is considered the world's greatest example of Mughal architecture and a symbol of eternal love. The British Raj from seventeen fifty-seven to nineteen forty-seven was British colonial rule that drained India's wealth, reshaped its governance and education, and unified its diverse regions under one administration. Mahatma Gandhi, from eighteen sixty-nine to nineteen forty-eight, led India's nonviolent independence movement against British rule, pioneering satyagraha, or truth-force, and influencing civil rights movements globally.

The caste system, an ancient Hindu social hierarchy, divided society by birth and occupation. Though outlawed in modern India, its legacy persists in cultural practice. India's connections to the world include Hinduism, the ancient religion and philosophy born and centered in India, Buddhism, the world religion founded in India by Siddhartha Gautama, the Vedas as foundational sacred texts, the Taj Mahal as architectural masterpiece, the British Raj as the colonial period, Gandhi as the independence leader, and the Silk Road as the trade route connecting India to China, Central Asia, and Europe.
